% three-column — reading order across three columns.
%
% One concern, two-column's at a width where line-by-line reading fails worse: each
% column holds about four words a line, so a reader that takes lines across the page
% makes sentences out of three unrelated ones. multicol balances the columns, which
% puts the first column break inside the second paragraph.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\usepackage{multicol}
\usepackage[paperwidth=6in,paperheight=3.4in,margin=0.5in]{geometry}
\pagestyle{empty}
% No hyphenation: that is the hyphenation fixture's concern.
\hyphenpenalty=10000 \exhyphenpenalty=10000 \sloppy
\begin{document}
\begin{multicols}{3}
The first paragraph starts the left column with a short account of a harbour town,
its fishing fleet, and the market held on the quay every morning.

The second paragraph follows the coast road east, past a lighthouse and two
coves, to a headland where the cliffs are tall enough to hide the sea from the road
and the wind is strong enough to bend every tree.

The third paragraph turns inland, along a lane between stone walls, to a village
with one church, one inn, and a green where the fair is held each summer.
\end{multicols}
\end{document}
